heading: Parks Commission Backs $3 Million Purchase Near Patrick Marsh
category: Sun Prairie Parks, Recreation and Forestry Commission
source: Parks, Recreation and Forestry Commission video · 0:13:36–0:38:39
summary: The Sun Prairie Parks, Recreation and Forestry Commission recommended buying about 107 acres next to Patrick Marsh for $3 million, contingent on Dane County grant approval. The city would use about $855,000 in park acquisition fees and seek county funding for the balance. City staff said the purchase would go to the City Council and that the Dane County Board was expected to consider the grant Dec. 17. Staff said public planning in 2027 could explore conservation, trail connections and other recreation uses.

heading: Parks Commission Backs Adopt-a-Park Pilot
category: Sun Prairie Parks, Recreation and Forestry Commission
source: Parks, Recreation and Forestry Commission video · 0:01:21–0:13:28
summary: The Sun Prairie Parks, Recreation and Forestry Commission recommended that the City Council approve an Adopt-a-Park program. Under the proposal, sponsors would commit to at least three years, pay an annual fee and complete one park cleanup each year. Staff would encourage additional volunteer hours and offer several sponsorship tiers. Staff said they hope to launch the program in 2027 and adjust it based on feedback from participants.

heading: Sun Prairie Invites Businesses to Join Fire and Lights Parade
category: Sun Prairie Parks, Recreation and Forestry Commission
source: Parks, Recreation and Forestry Commission video · 0:39:48–0:40:40
summary: Sun Prairie staff said the city is accepting vendors for its Nov. 28 Fire and Lights Parade. Businesses can participate by decorating their trucks. Staff said opening the parade to business vehicles will help when the holiday weekend or bad weather makes it harder for fire trucks to take part.

heading: Wisconsin and FTC Announce Proposed $63 Million Family Dollar Settlement
summary: Wisconsin Attorney General Josh Kaul, the Federal Trade Commission and 16 other states announced a proposed $63 million settlement with Family Dollar. The regulators allege the retailer routinely charged shoppers more at checkout than the prices shown on shelves, tags and advertisements. The proposed order would establish a $40 million fund for eligible consumers and a $20 million discount program for customers. It would also require Family Dollar to put a pricing accuracy program in place and have it independently assessed each year.

heading: Wisconsin Reports Second Death Linked to Measles Outbreak
summary: The Wisconsin Department of Health Services and the Grant County Health Department reported a child's death associated with measles, the second death linked to the state's 2026 outbreak. State health officials reported 649 cases in 20 counties since August as of Nov. 13, the state's highest case count in more than 35 years. The department said it is working with local and Tribal health agencies to track cases, support testing and make more vaccine doses available.
